messages:
maya: FYI noticed a weird oscillation on the kernel selector when tool pauses are ~30-200ms. throughput spikes then drops every ~8s.
sahil: can you paste the perf profile? sounds like kernel churn.
maya: gist: https://short.internal/g/abc123 (flame graph + trace). Quick snippet from the trace:
```
[2026-03-17T18:02:13Z] batch_size=24 -> kernel=A (fp16-optimized)
[2026-03-17T18:02:21Z] tool pause start (user fn), queue growth + kv miss
[2026-03-17T18:02:22Z] batch_size=6 -> kernel=B (small-seq path)
[2026-03-17T18:02:21..30Z] KV cache miss spikes x4, latency +30ms
```
chen: hmm that aligns with our kernel scoring heuristic picking kernels by expected seq len and batch mass. If a tool pause splits one large batch into smaller fragments, kernel B (higher overhead) gets picked and costs us.
ryan: did we log token_budget targets for those requests? might be that budget estimation is stale for structured outputs with stop tokens.
maya: right — these are structured output flows (json schema + toolcall) where stop tokens cause early termination, but the scheduler doesn't re-eval when a tool pause returns. We end up with fragmented batches running suboptimal kernels.
sahil: infra-bot, can we get recent kernel selection metrics for the last 30m for model rwd-v2-small? infra-bot: scheduled, fetching.
infra-bot: done. metrics snapshot: kernel_switch_rate=0.62/s, avg_batch_size=11.8 -> during incidents avg_batch_size dips to 5.2, throughput -28%, p95 latency +42%.
chen: two actionable ideas:
  1) add a short re-eval window on tool return (100ms soft) to avoid picking a different kernel for recently-fragmented batches.
  2) tighten token_budget estimation for structured outputs: inspect stop-token probability and reduce predicted tail tokens by 20% when toolcall flagged.
maya: +1 on both. re-eval window prevents kernel thrash; tighter token_budget avoids creating small batches in the first place.
ryan: what about KV cache behavior? the trace shows cache misses during the pause which makes the new kernel heavier.
chen: yes, when a function call executes we temporarily evict streaming KV slots because we prioritise memory for tool stacks. That eviction increases recompute when the batch resumes.
sahil: suggestion: pin KV page ranges for pinned-inflight sessions (small mem reserve) so toolcalls don't evict active context. cost: small mem uplift per session.
maya: can we prototype: (a) 100ms re-eval window, (b) token_budget adjust for toolcall, (c) KV pinning flag for sessions with structured-output?
ryan: prototype plan OK. timeline? sahil?
sahil: I'll scope. estimate: perf patch + unit tests 2d, runtime rollout 1d canary, observe 72h.
chen: quick perf check commands I used:
```
# sample kernel selector log
curl -s http://localhost:9001/debug/selector?span=60 | jq .hist
# or run local replay
PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/perf/test-toolpause_replay.py -k reeval
```
maya: after applying a naive 150ms re-eval in a staging run, kernel_switch_rate dropped 38% and p95 latency recovered ~18% in the replay.
infra-bot: canary rollout scheduled to eng-runtime-staging at 2034568200 with rollback on kernel_switch_rate > 0.5/s or p95 > +20%.
ryan: one more thought — we should log a flag in traces when a batch resumes after a tool pause so we can measure fragmentation downstream.
sahil: good call. add trace tag "resume_after_toolpause".
maya: i'll open a PR with the three changes + tests. tagging owners @sahil @chen.
chen: thanks, will review.
ryan: if this reduces kernel churn we might also lower cost by 3-6% for these workflows. small win but stable.
maya: cool. will update thread when PR links available. :rocket:
